text:
maria: Seeing a weird spike of client requests from APAC that resolve AAAA but then just sit in SYN_RECV / time out. p50 fine, p99 for inference backend jumps ~400ms for a subset. Noticed LB health checks flapping for the same backends. Anyone else?

ben: I saw that too, started around 02:14 UTC. More common from mobile carriers. Looks like some clients prefer IPv6 and our edge returned AAAA. But NAT64 translation isn't being used for those flows?

lee: Can you paste the LB probe logs? I'm wondering if probes come in on v6 and backend replies are only v4-routed.

maria: Logs below (sanitized):
```
[2026-05-09T02:14:23Z] lb-probe edge-nyc-1 client_ip=2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334 probe=healthcheck path=/hc status=timeout backend=svc-inference-07
[2026-05-09T02:14:24Z] lb-probe edge-nyc-2 client_ip=198.51.100.42 probe=healthcheck path=/hc status=200 backend=svc-inference-07
```
So same backend healthy for v4 probes, timing out on v6 probes.

sri: That looks like asymmetric routing at the egress or we have no proper NAT64 prefixes advertised to that edge-pop. Do we see any nat64/64:ff9b:: entries in the edge's route table?

ben: Quick check from an affected node: `ip -6 route` shows only link-local and ::/0 via our internal fabric, no explicit nat64 route. But DNS64 runs in control plane for some regions — maybe it's only enabled in APAC compute region, not edge-nyc?

maria: Reproduced locally with curl from a client sim: `curl --ipv6 -v https://api.redwood.ai/health` hangs at TCP handshake. `traceroute -6` shows our edge LB accepts SYN but backend reply has source v4 and gets dropped.

lee: Classic: LB is dualstack and returns AAAA, but health probes arrive on v6 and our backend pool only has v4 endpoints or expects NAT64 translation. If the node doesn't translate, replies never make it back.

claire: Oncall note: this is impacting a small % of requests but p99 for those customers goes up. No customer-facing outage yet. Should we remove AAAA records from the edge DNS for now?

ben: I propose a short mitigation: 1) stop advertising AAAA for edge-nyc zone (DNS change, TTL 30s) 2) add tcpdump on LB (filter 'tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0 and dst port 443') to capture v6 client IPs 3) patch route table to include NAT64 prefix for the fabric if we want long-term.

maria: Agreed. Rolling DNS TTL change now. Patch queued: `dnsctl update --zone=edge-nyc --remove-aaaa --ttl=30`

infra-bot: dnsctl: change submitted (id=chg-6821) by maria — propagation expected ~30s.

lee: Started tcpdump on lb-edge-03: `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'ip6 and tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0 and port 443' -w /tmp/v6syn.pcap`

sri: Also adding a quick iptables NAT64 rule on a single canary node to validate translation path before we roll fabric-wide. I'll open a RFC and a canary play.

maria: DNS change propagated, monitoring. Early signs: v6 probe timeouts dropped to zero in the last 40s.

claire: Good. Follow-ups: (1) audit region-wise DNS64/NAT64 config (2) ensure load balancer healthcheck uses same address family as backends or use v4-only probes for mixed pools (3) add an integration test for dualstack probe-paths.

ben: Filing infra ticket with logs + pcap: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-8421 — assigned to @sri.

maria: Thanks all. I'll keep an eye on latency for impacted customers and post an update in 30m. :thumbsup:
